title: Let's put the AI in lots of little boxes - Kenton Varda, Cloudflare Connect 2025
summary: Varda argues that AI-generated and agent code should run in lightweight sandboxes with narrow, code-level capability interfaces rather than relying on model judgment.

assertions.quote: They can uh call more complicated interfaces when they're calling code than when they're calling tools.

verdicts.note: Cloudflare and Anthropic report token and accuracy gains from code-execution tool use, but the evidence is mostly vendor-reported and task-dependent.

assertions.quote: what if this scam email starts to contain prompt injection attacks? Like we haven't figured out how to defend against those yet.
we need to take a a uh uh technical approach to preventing them from making these mistakes.
there's an important class of problems that you cannot see by just looking at it which is security bugs
you have to already understand as a human everything that it does uh and you are responsible if there's a problem
That agent cannot leak any secrets because the only thing it knows are things that the recipients of anything it sends already know.

verdicts.note: Information-flow designs such as dual-LLM and CaMeL can provably limit leakage, but they cost functionality and do not stop every kind of misuse.

assertions.quote: There is no way to issue an OOTH token that gives access to a single uh email in a Gmail inbox.

verdicts.note: Major APIs such as Gmail offer broad scopes that cannot express per-item agent permissions, though some APIs have finer-grained scopes.
